title: Inequality chain proving n < 7 for IMO 2019 Q4
intent: Reduce IMO 2019 Q4 from infinitely many candidate pairs (k, n) to a finite search over n in {1..6} by proving the bound n < 7 through one 'also ... finally' inequality chain whose three non-trivial links are the named same-file lemmas k_gt_T, rhs_less and fact_ge_power.

children.name: k_gt_T
children.closed_by: an 'also ... finally' chain T = multiplicity 2 rhs = legendre_aux k 2 < k; links multiplicity_2_rhs (simp), multiplicity_prime_fact, legendre_aux_less

children.name: rhs_less
children.closed_by: an 'also ... finally' chain rhs = 2^T * prod (2^i - 1) < ... = 2 ^ n^2; links rhs_altdef, prod_mono_strict, power_sum

children.name: fact_ge_power
children.statement: fact_ge_power: "fact n >= c ^ n" (from "fact n0 >= c ^ n0", "c <= n0 + 1", "n >= n0")
children.closed_by: proof (induction n rule: dec_induct); the step case closes by mult_mono then simp

applicability.goal_shape: a bound like n < N, or more generally an inequality between two expressions, that can be pushed through a chain of named inequalities so that its truth collapses to a small finite check (here n in {1..6})
applicability.use_when: the goal is a chain of inequalities whose individual steps are non-trivial enough to each deserve a named lemma (each with its own proof), and the whole chain can be written as 'also ... finally' so transitivity is automatic; the steps are ordered < / <= / = in one direction
applicability.avoid_when: the steps are one-off rewrites with no reuse (fold them inline); a direct proof by induction or a single library theorem is shorter; the chain needs >= steps, which Isar's 'also' does not compose by default

claims.claim: The parent n_less_7 closes from its three named children: k_gt_T supplies fact T <= fact k (lines 245-246), rhs_less supplies rhs < 2 ^ n^2 (line 248), fact_ge_power supplies fact T >= 8 ^ T (line 258), and the proof ends in qed (line 260); each child also ends in qed (lines 38, 191, 224).

thys/IMO2019 contains no sorry, admit or oops: a grep for 'sorry', 'admit' and 'oops' over the three theories IMO2019_Q1.thy, IMO2019_Q4.thy and IMO2019_Q5.thy at the pinned commit returned no matches.

The glue proof spans 29 lines (232-260) and calls 3 named same-file lemmas directly (direct_lemmas = 3); the longest chain of project lemmas below the main theorem has depth 3, via n_less_7 -> k_gt_T -> multiplicity_2_rhs -> rhs_altdef; child proof lines are 11 (k_gt_T, 181-191), 18 (rhs_less, 207-224) and 7 (fact_ge_power, 32-38).
claims.evidence: line ranges counted in https://github.com/isabelle-prover/mirror-afp-devel/blob/07cd9ca548d180f234c63f06bf5d1cb85c7fc5df/thys/IMO2019/IMO2019_Q4.thy: glue L232-L260, k_gt_T L181-L191, rhs_less L207-L224, fact_ge_power L32-L38, multiplicity_2_rhs L160-L174, rhs_altdef L144-L155

claims.claim: The authors state the plan in the comment before the lemma: 'It is clear that 2^(n^2) <= 8^T and that 8^T < T! if T is sufficiently big ... We can therefore conclude that n must be less than 7.'

The same 'also ... finally'-over-named-lemmas pattern recurs at the child level: k_gt_T (lines 181-191) chains multiplicity_2_rhs, multiplicity_prime_fact and legendre_aux_less, and rhs_less (lines 207-224) chains over rhs_altdef.

metrics.how_counted: glue_lines = proof body of n_less_7, lines 232-260; child proof lines = 181-191 (k_gt_T), 207-224 (rhs_less), 32-38 (fact_ge_power); depth = longest project-lemma chain n_less_7 -> k_gt_T -> multiplicity_2_rhs -> rhs_altdef

consequences: The move creates one obligation per link: each named lemma must be proved in its own right before the chain composes them. Transitivity of the chain is discharged automatically by 'also'/'finally'. A link stated too weak breaks the final result (here the strict < survives only because rhs_less is strict after the equality fact T = rhs). fact_bounds needs T >= 21, so the glue first derives T >= 21 from n >= 7; forgetting that precondition leaves fact T >= 8^T without a hypothesis.
